problem: Existing dialogue-enabled navigation methods consume oracle answers as transient text context for immediate decisions, so information is lost once the agent moves to a new room or branch. End-to-end learned methods also leave the dialogue-to-state conversion implicit and uninspectable.
motivation: In Interactive Instance Goal Navigation (IIGN), category-level instructions leave both instance uncertainty and exploration uncertainty. Answers are only useful if they are grounded, retained and reused across a long-horizon episode. This motivates turning dialogue into persistent spatial and object-centric state.
key_idea: Compile oracle answers into persistent structured memory (target facts, route/history corridor masks on a graph, and object-candidate labels) that a unified zero-shot policy uses for frontier ranking and target approach.
insight: Persistent state matters more than raw dialogue volume. One information question already lifts SR from 11.6 to 20.6 and gives the best MSP. Removing the route bonus causes the largest drop among the value-prior ablations (SR 25.4 to 19.0), so route-grounded memory is the strongest spatial prior. Removing the similarity verifier raises OS to 70.0 but drops SPL to 11.02 and doubles steps, so reaching target-like regions does not suffice without persistent instance-state verification.
method: Structured maps: value map (VLFM/BLIP-2 frontier value), topological graph from skeletonization, room map (watershed + VLM labels, target-relevant room), object map (GroundingDINO+MobileSAM point clouds associated by KD-tree)
Entropy-aware detection: a VLM yes/no/unknown answer's next-token logits give entropy H; a proposal is accepted only if the answer is yes and H<tau_H

Similarity-based instance verification: the VLM describes the candidate, an LLM refines the evidence against target facts F_tar, and a similarity score is mapped by two thresholds to rejected/pending/confirmed labels

Active questioning: information questions (episode start / insufficient facts), route questions (at unqueried branch nodes when nothing is confirmed), disambiguation questions (close, stable pending candidates; oracle answers yes iff the target is in view within 3 m)

Route-answer grounding: bounded DFS path proposals with branch-balanced Top-B selection, an LLM matcher picks the path, and a route session gives a short-term corridor plus a decaying history corridor

Frontier scoring: s(xi)=value x route mask (Gaussian, beta_r=3.0) x history mask (beta_h=0.5, gamma=0.8) x room prior (0.25); pending candidates trigger a waypoint approach and confirmed ones trigger PointGoal navigation

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5 (VLM/LLM, frozen) + GroundingDINO + MobileSAM + BLIP-2-style value matcher
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose estimate + dialogue history
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30° left/right / ASK / STOP
setting.privileged: oracle answers to questions (privileged access to target attributes, location and scene structure), as defined by the IIGN task; no GT map or pose otherwise

numbers.extra: unlimited oracle question budget, avg 4.58 questions

numbers_note: The paper does not name the split; val-unseen is assumed for unseen scenes. The benchmark is VL-LN IIGN, which is not in the canonical list.
results: On VL-LN IIGN, SAIN-D reaches SR 25.4, SPL 14.17 and NE 8.06 without policy training, beating the trained VLLN-D (20.2 / 13.07 / 8.84). A single information question (SAIN-D1) already matches VLLN-D on SR (20.6). Failure analysis shows wrong detections falling from 48.0% to 24.9% with dialogue.
limitations: Ambiguity/instance verification remains the main bottleneck (51.2% of failures under SAIN-D), and OS is lower than that of VLLN-D
Relies on an oracle that answers accurately and on external VLM/LLM calls over HTTP, with many hand-set hyperparameters; SAIN-D needs 4.58 questions on average
Real-world evidence is a qualitative demonstration; quantitative real-world results are only in the supplementary video
